PullRequest.Title: Move new session composer layout above vs below chat input
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Fixes `sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout` so it only changes the new-session composer:

- moves the existing Workspace, Worktree, and Branch controls into a row immediately above the input
- keeps the Copilot/harness picker pinned to the right of that row, including on web
- keeps the model picker inside the new-session input and mode/permissions below it
- preserves the original running-session composer: Agent/model inside the input, mode/permissions in the secondary row below
- leaves chat-tip eligibility and rendering unchanged
- leaves Agent Host repository menu eligibility unchanged
- preserves the removal of the contextual new-session heading from `main`

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- targeted ESLint and Stylelint
- 171 focused Chromium browser tests
- live Code OSS Agents window verification with the experimental settings enabled
  - new-session workspace row is 4px above the input; permissions remain below it
  - running-session primary input contains Agent/model only
  - running-session mode/permissions render in a separate 22px secondary row below the input
  - Workspace and permissions controls share the same left edge
  - repository controls use the same 11px label role and 12px compact codicon tier as permissions

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and render the new-session composer with the experimental layout enabled, including workspace, repository, harness, model, mode, and permission controls.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Synchronous DOM construction, menu-toolbar creation, and responsive picker measurement must complete before the composer is usable. The diff keeps one NewSessionControl toolbar but creates it directly in the lower controls row, leaves workspace controls in their original host, and uses CSS for placement instead of the removed autorun-driven DOM moves.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled composer controls and configuration/quick-chat state changes; realistically a small fixed number of pickers, not repositories or sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread render; responsive layout is observer-driven and serialized by its _isLayouting guard. No new task fan-out, queue, or concurrent expensive work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache key, cold/warm cache, coalescing, or negative-cache behavior changes. Menu/context state is local and the same picker instances are constructed as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed render code, toolbar ownership, autorun removal, and responsive-layout delegates were traced directly; none adds an expensive operation or raises execution frequency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact layout cost depends on enabled picker count and viewport width, but effective cardinality is a small fixed set of composer controls. The diff removes dynamic relocation and an extra primary-lane traversal rather than adding scaling work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new layout avoids the prior experiment-specific workspace/session-control reparenting and related relayout calls while preserving a single toolbar and existing repository-control relocation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change experimental-layout, unified-workspace-picker, or quick-chat state while the new-session composer is open.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The surviving NewChatWidget autorun toggles one CSS class and may move the existing repository-control node, then invokes the existing secondary responsive layout. The removed NewChatInput autorun previously also moved workspace and session-control nodes and synchronously laid out both responsive lanes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of relevant configuration/session-state transitions and the fixed control set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable reactions run synchronously and serially on the UI thread. Repository controls are one grouped toolbar; there is no per-repository fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration observables retain existing event filtering. No new cache or miss behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: before/after behavior is explicit in the deleted autorun and unchanged repository placement call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Configuration and quick-chat transitions are user-driven and infrequent; repository-menu cardinality varies by provider but remains represented by one toolbar relocation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff reduces synchronous DOM writes and responsive relayout work on state changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, resize, and type in a running Agent Host session composer.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Running-session picker controls now remain in ChatInputSecondary for all layouts. The diff removes experiment-specific context-usage-widget reparenting, trailing editor-space updates, context-key/config listeners, and the extra width subtraction from the editor layout path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Resize events and input content/layout changes, with a fixed number of running-session controls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread layout/input path; picker menu rendering is local and serialized. The contribution now registers one action-view factory per running-session picker instead of factories for both primary and secondary menus.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes. Existing editor dimension caching and layout guards remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the deleted ChatView listeners and changed ChatInputPart width calculation directly establish the before/after path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Resize and content-change frequency varies, but the changed mechanism removes work from these hot paths rather than adding it.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR narrows the experiment and removes experiment-specific UI-thread work from running sessions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Populate and display Agent Host mode/approval/configuration picker actions for running sessions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Contribution startup registers action-view factories and menu items; picker view items are instantiated only for the visible secondary toolbar. Provider/session menu refresh listeners remain unchanged.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed picker-action count plus existing provider/session menu state.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous contribution/menu registration with no asynchronous fan-out. The diff reduces registrations from two menu locations to one for each running-session picker.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No provider cache, session cache, or invalidation behavior changes. Existing provider/session refresh ownership is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all changed registrations and menu predicates were inspected, and they reduce duplicate surfaces without changing refresh boundaries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider count and visible-session count can vary, but the changed lines do not add refresh iterations or picker instances.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Registration and rendering cardinality are reduced or unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 13 changed files and every diff page. Traced new-session render/configuration transitions, running-session input/layout, responsive picker measurement, and Agent Host picker registration. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or concrete regression fix requiring blame was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
